DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers about railroad crossings ahead. Drive carefully when you see this sign.

questions.question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road with traffic moving in both directions.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive poorly, just like drunk drivers. Opening a window, playing loud music, or drinking coffee is not enough to fix drowsiness.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: If you might hit another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may confuse or scare them. Yield to them and drive safely.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is about to hit you?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers when they may not see you and could hit you.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in construction zones?
questions.explanation: In Oklahoma, fines for traffic violations in construction zones are doubled when workers are present and warning signs are posted.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Immediately pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Release the accelerator and slow down. Keep both hands on the wheel and steer gently back onto the road. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: What is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment

questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch closely for workers and machines.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Do not return to your original lane until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when slowing down, stopping, or changing direction. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Always signal your lane change in advance, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on country roads if no sign is posted?
questions.explanation: The speed limit on country roads is 55 miles per hour unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow posted speed limits when they appear.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers travel too fast for the conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far. Increase your following distance to give yourself more time to stop if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. Use your headlights properly.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the road shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights stopped to pick up or drop off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and wait as long as the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What do orange-colored signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones where people are working on or near the highway. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols to warn drivers.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet directly behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them. Do not tailgate large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.
